summary.oneLiner: Chennai-rooted jewellery house since 1971, operating an asset-light wholesale (B2B) and retail (B2C) model across gold, diamond and precious-stone jewellery, now scaling a premium diamond brand (Vajraa) and retail footprint.
summary.business: Khazanchi Jewellers is engaged in the wholesale and retail sale of gold jewellery, diamond jewellery and precious stone jewellery, built on an integrated model of sourcing, in-house design, manufacturing partnerships and retail operations. Wholesale (B2B) is the stable, cash-generating core serving more than 1,000 clients across India through an asset-light model using authorised partner manufacturers, while retail (B2C) is a smaller but faster-growing, higher-margin channel anchored by a new flagship showroom in Chennai.

currentContext.strengths: More than five decades of operating history with deep industry relationships and established customer trust|Extensive in-house jewellery design repository of over 5 lakh designs, enabling differentiation across geographies and occasions|Asset-light manufacturing model, working through authorised partner manufacturers rather than owning production|Strong wholesale distribution network serving 1,000+ B2B clients across India|Growing retail brand presence anchored by a flagship 10,000 sq. ft. showroom and a film-actress brand ambassador
currentContext.strategies: Grow the retail channel toward a ₹500 Crore sales target by opening new showrooms, expanding the Vajraa Diamonds range, and shifting further toward higher-margin products|Scale Vajraa Diamonds, the dedicated diamond/studded jewellery brand, to address higher-value consumers and improve blended margins as it grows|Launch dedicated digital platforms for B2B trade and B2C e-commerce to extend reach from a regional to a national base|Deepen its network of wholesale customers and manufacturing partners to reinforce its position within the jewellery ecosystem|Continue investing in design-led differentiation, adopting advanced manufacturing technologies (3D-printed paper casting, electro forming, laser cutting, AI-enabled production) to strengthen its design capabilities|Prepare for migration from the BSE SME platform to the Main Board, with eligibility due in August 2026|Compete on premiumisation through the Vajraa brand and its brand ambassador, targeting higher-value consumers and expanding presence in value-added categories|The Board recommended a final dividend for FY26 subject to shareholder approval, governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy. The Board decided not to transfer any amount to general reserve, choosing instead to retain the entire FY26 profit within the business to fund growth (reinvestment-led capital allocation over reserve build-up).
currentContext.expansion: Khazanchi's recent expansion has been retail-led rather than manufacturing-led, consistent with its asset-light model (manufacturing is outsourced to authorised partner manufacturers). In FY2021-22 the Company entered into an agreement to purchase land to establish a new flagship showroom; this culminated in the opening of a 10,000 sq. ft. flagship showroom in Chennai (Walltax Road, Sowcarpet) on February 7, 2026, bringing the gold, diamond, antique, temple, Calcutta and Vajraa collections together under one roof. During FY26 the Company also launched its new diamond jewellery brand 'VAJRAA DIAMONDS - BY KHAZANCHI', its entry into the premium/studded diamond segment. Looking ahead, management intends to open further new showrooms to strengthen the retail footprint, expand the Vajraa Diamonds range, and launch dedicated B2B trade and B2C e-commerce platforms to extend reach nationally.
currentContext.mdna: Wholesale remains the stable, cash-generating core that funds the company's retail and premium expansion, while retail and Vajraa Diamonds are the main levers for margin improvement through a richer product mix|Retail carries higher making charges and more pricing power than wholesale, making growth in this channel central to margin improvement|Organised retail's share of India's jewellery market has risen to about a third to ~40% (from ~22% a few years ago), driven by mandatory BIS hallmarking and HUID adoption pushing the shift from unorganised to branded retail|Wedding and festive demand is described as the single largest, most durable demand pillar anchoring footfall and ticket size across every region and season|Rising disposable incomes, urbanization and wedding demand are fuelling Tier II and Tier III city growth, seen as an opportunity for the B2B business|Industry-wide technology adoption (omni-channel retail, AI-driven engagement, CRM and ERP systems) is reshaping competition|Silver is flagged industry-wide as one of the fastest-growing jewellery categories, led by younger buyers, though the company's own silver plans are not detailed in this section|Industry value growth is moderating gently (~12-16% expected in FY26 versus ~14-18% in FY25) off a high FY2024 base, but rising average ticket sizes and premium mix are expected to keep revenue climbing even if volumes soften|Real GDP growth of 7.7% and rising private consumption (7.7%) and gross fixed capital formation (8.2%) are supporting discretionary spending on gold and jewellery|Record gold prices during the year did not dent demand; exchange of old gold accounted for an estimated 40-60% of jewellery transactions across retailers|India accounted for 22% of global jewellery demand and remains the world's second-largest jewellery market, a favourable long-term backdrop|Studded and diamond jewellery is gaining share (estimated at 15-20% of the market) as customers move toward design-led pieces, supporting the Vajraa positioning|Long-term sector outlook is supported by 100% FDI under the automatic route, growing organised-retail investment, and trade agreements (India-UAE CEPA, India-UK FTA) expected to enhance export competitiveness|Retail footprint remains concentrated in South India, limiting brand visibility elsewhere, while national jewellery chains are expanding aggressively into the region|Business remains working-capital intensive with debt-to-equity rising during the year (0.28x to 0.35x), a factor management flags as a challenge alongside gold price volatility and regulatory change risk (import duty, GST, hallmarking rules)

risks.note: Gold and precious metals are the largest part of inventory and procurement cost; price volatility affects inventory values and margins. Mitigated by planning procurement against demand forecasts, keeping inventory tight, and opportunistic forward buying during price corrections.
The sector is subject to evolving rules on hallmarking, GST, import duty and KYC norms; changes in these rules can disrupt cost structures and operations.

The market is consolidating and national jewellery chains are expanding aggressively into South India, the Company's core market; it competes on design library depth, showroom experience and premium positioning (Vajraa, brand ambassador).
The business is working-capital intensive due to high gold inventory and seasonal demand; debt-to-equity rose from 0.28x to 0.35x during the year as current borrowings increased to fund inventory.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration in Tamil Nadu / South India
risks.note: Tamil Nadu accounted for 75% of FY26 revenue and the retail footprint remains concentrated in South India, limiting brand visibility elsewhere even as other states' contribution has been rising.

Retail is still a small part of total revenue (10% in FY26) compared with wholesale (90%), even though retail earns better margins, leaving profitability still heavily dependent on the lower-margin wholesale channel.
An economic slowdown or sustained inflation could reduce discretionary spending on jewellery, a category management explicitly flags as a threat.
